newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill auction yield dips below 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill auction yield dips below 19 pct.

text.p: The average yield on Russian Treasury bills at auction fell below 19 percent on Wednesday but dealers said a shortage of funds in the market would prevent prices from advancing much further on Thursday.

The series 21080 364-day GKO Treasury bills maturing July 22, 1998, yielded an average 18.89 percent at the over-subscribed auction, raising 5.88 trillion roubles cash for the finance ministry out of 9.00 trillion on offer.

At an auction of 364-day paper a week earlier, the average yield was 19.20 percent. But market yields had already dipped below 19 percent, with last week's issue closing on Tuesday at a yield of 18.92.

Dealers forecast prices would change little on Thursday as banks had little money left for tomorrow's trading, after a shortage of roubles on the interbank market drove overnight funds up to 80 percent.

"We are unlikely to see more than two trillion roubles in the trading system and that is why prices will not change a lot," said Vneshtorgbank dealer Sergei Fyodorov. "I think that the yield will fluctuate in the 18-19 percent range."

At another auction the finance ministry sold a 728-day OFZ interest-bearing bond at a price in line with market expectations helped by a high-volume single bid at a non-competitive price, dealers said on Wednesday.

Dealers said the large bid appeared to be from state-owned Sberbank, Russia's biggest institution and a major player on the market. There was no comment from Sberbank, which often acts in the market on behalf of the authorities.
The average price of the 728-day bond was 96.80 percent, and dealers had forecast it in a 96.12-97.24 percent.

The finance ministry's total proceeds from the auctions and subsequent sales of bonds in a post-auction trading session was 9.66 trillion roubles, while interest payements and securities repayments, including the early repayment of a tax-free OFZ bond on a voluntary basis, were 9.34 trillion.
